findings.note: Primary sponsor (with one other member) of House Bill 825, Election Improvements, filed 2025-04-08, referred to the House Rules committee 2025-04-09, no further action. Text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/HTML/H825v1.html) changes absentee-ballot requests: the request form would ask for the last four digits of the Social Security number plus a driver license number, special ID card number or date of birth, and the State Board rules on returned absentee ballots would allow an alternative affidavit when a voter cannot attach an ID photocopy. The same bill also bans ranked choice voting, shortens early voting and adjusts rules on activity near polling places.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (vote 66 to 47, passed)
findings.note: Voted aye on second reading of House Bill 958, Election Law Changes. The ratified text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/HTML/H958v9.html) requires a voter registration application to affirmatively state US citizenship before it is processed, has the State Board create a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens from a federal database, and also changes precinct-official, deceased-voter list and campaign-finance rules. On 2026-08-04 the final concurrence vote is recorded as an excused absence for this member, and the bill page shows a Governor's veto.

findings.note: HB 825 'Election Improvements', listed with Scott as a primary sponsor alongside Echevarria. The filed text changes what an absentee-ballot request and a reasonable-impediment affidavit must contain: the last four digits of the Social Security number plus one of a driver license number, a non-operator ID number, or date of birth. The bill also bans ranked choice voting and cuts early voting. It was sent to a House committee and did not advance.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, second reading (66-47). Scott is listed among the Ayes.
findings.note: Legislative staff summary of Part II of the ratified bill: it requires DMV to send full Social Security numbers to the State Board of Elections monthly, requires the State Board to set a process to remove non-citizens from voter rolls using federal database information, and bars processing a registration application unless the applicant affirmatively says they are a U.S. citizen (with a sworn form if the question is left blank). The Governor vetoed it on 2026-08-17.
